matches.rationale: Finding 10 identifies that Introduction cites [39] for the Mixture-of-Time module while [39] is a forecast verification framework, matching the ground-truth fabrication of a reference to support the MoT methodology.

No finding describes the logical inconsistency in Equation (4) where softmax-normalized scores are linearly mixed with raw scores, reusing V in a contradictory way. Findings 6-8 address different method-logic issues.

The ground truth highlights two problems: contradictory data-year statements and filtering of high-MAE observations before evaluation. Findings 1-2 capture the inconsistent training/test periods and potential leakage, while findings 3-4 explicitly describe the undisclosed filtering against HYCOM, together covering the experimental protocol deficiency.

The ground truth attacks the 'first... model achieving six-hourly global ocean forecast' novelty claim with prior studies [43,46]. No finding contests this 'first' claim; finding 11 questions sub-daily superiority evidence, not the priority assertion.
The ground truth asserts Figure 4's performance margins are physically implausible and suggests cherry-picking. No finding directly addresses the implausibility of the RMSE gap or Figure 4.

Finding 11 identifies that the conclusion's claim of superior sub-daily performance over operational models is unsupported by observational evidence, matching the ground-truth rhetorical exaggeration and omission of limitations in the Conclusion.

The ground truth concerns overstatement of multi-step loss efficacy versus observed error accumulation. No finding discusses multi-step loss training or its inconsistency with Figure 2/5 error growth.
The ground truth flags missing uncertainty quantification. No finding mentions absence of confidence intervals, error bounds, or uncertainty quantification.
The ground truth points to missing justification for selecting only 20 vertical layers out of 40 down to 5,000 m. No finding addresses the vertical layer selection or its narrative inconsistency.

Finding 9 detects an editorial comment about inconsistent RMSE units/scales for salinity and temperature in Figure 5, matching the ground-truth issue of questionable salinity errors and inconsistent axis conventions in the same ablation figure.

Finding 11 points out the Abstract's 'superior performance' claim lacks sub-daily validations, matching the ground-truth rhetorical exaggeration of 'superior skill' and 'state-of-the-art performance' in the Abstract.
The ground truth concerns omission of comprehensive risk/ethics discussion in the Appendix regarding training on imperfect reanalysis data. No finding addresses this ethical omission.
The ground truth criticizes selective presentation of spatial error maps in Figure 2 that downplay high-error regions. No finding discusses Figure 2 or selective spatial error reporting.
The ground truth identifies an unreported training-design issue of batch size 1 per GPU yielding effective batch size 4. No finding mentions batch size or training stability concerns.

The ground truth points to an unfair comparison in Appendix Table 1 between FuXi-Ocean trained on older data (2006-2014) and models trained on data reaching 2020/2021. Findings about training-period inconsistencies (1,2) do not address this cross-model temporal mismatch.

The ground truth targets overgeneralization in the Conclusion that 6-hour forecasts confirm effectiveness across all ocean variables and scales. Finding 11 concerns lack of sub-daily validation evidence, not blanket claims about all variables/scales.

The ground truth objects to the assertion that errors remain within 'operational tolerance thresholds' in western boundary currents, which downplays deficiencies. No finding mentions this specific rhetorical downplaying.
